# Cully v0.10.0

Cully now watches the whole coding session, not only what it remembers: a session journal, timeline, replay, handoff and rescue, an Agent Health panel in the terminal, and sessions with tasks in memory. It works the same for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor.

- `cully run AGENT` starts Claude Code, Codex, `cursor-agent` or any executable in the Cully terminal, with an Agent Health bar and a panel that shows each agent's own model, tokens and limits. `cully claude`, `cully codex` and `cully cursor` are shortcuts.
- A local session journal, fed by tool-event hooks, records time, agent, kind of tool, pass or fail and a one-way command hash. It never records prompts, file contents, command arguments or output. Run `cully setup` again to install the new Claude Code and Cursor hooks.
- `cully timeline`, `cully replay` (steps, file hotspots, `--json`, offline `--html`), `cully handoff` and `cully rescue` read that journal. `cully status` adds a measured health block with loop detection.
- Memory gains sessions and tasks: migration 004 is additive, `cully_session` and `cully_session_get` are new MCP tools, and `clear_task` unlinks a session's task while keeping the record. Run the data image's `migrate` command before serving traffic.
- Both deployment manifests now gate all eleven MCP tools, and a contract test keeps registration, manifests and the skill in agreement.
- Internal: one agent catalog replaces scattered per-agent switches and shared Codex-named code uses neutral names. On-disk paths, hook commands and panel output are unchanged.

Known issues: the Claude and Cursor panels still show some Codex wording in their tips, and `TestCodexPaneStopsOnTerminalHangup` fails on at least one macOS machine.
